candidates.change_summary: Remove the overflow check requirement, making the function always revert.
Remove the balance increment, so deposited funds are lost and balance remains unchanged.
Increment the balance of a fixed address instead of the caller, changing the balance mapping key.
Delete the revert statement so that MinSum can be changed after initialization.
Replace the revert condition with a no-op so MinSum is always updated regardless of initialized state.
Replace assignment to MinSum with a constant value, so MinSum is always set to 0 instead of the input.
Always assign MinSum before checking the guard, so that even if the guard reverts, MinSum has already been changed.
Change the guard to revert if NOT initialized, altering when MinSum can be set.
Insert an early return before the assignment so that MinSum is never updated.
Change the Collect balance guard from checking msg.sender's balance to checking the zero address's balance, preventing normal callers from ever collecting.
Change the Collect amount guard to compare against MinSum instead of _am, allowing collection when the balance is at least MinSum.
Change the balance subtraction to an addition, increasing the caller's balance by _am on collection.
Change the external call success guard to always run the log update regardless of call success, so failed value transfers do not revert.
Move the caller's balance subtraction from before the external call to after it, exposing stale balance during reentrancy.
Change the Collect guard from `balances[msg.sender] >= MinSum` to `balances[msg.sender] > MinSum`, reverting when a caller has exactly MinSum and otherwise permitting the call.
Change the second Collect guard from `balances[msg.sender] >= _am` to `balances[msg.sender] > _am`, reverting on an exact-balance withdrawal that the original allows.
Replace the subtraction update `balances[msg.sender] - _am` with `balances[msg.sender] + _am`, so a successful Collect increases the recorded balance instead of decreasing it.
Invert the post-call check from `if(_veri_ok)` to `if(!_veri_ok)`, causing the transaction to revert when the external call succeeds and to succeed without logging when it fails.
Move the balance subtraction from before the external call to immediately after it, so the callee observes the old balance during the call and reentrancy can double-spend.
Delete the `Log.AddMessage(msg.sender,_am,"Collect")` statement on the success path, so a successful Collect no longer records a log message.
